target_customer: Small service businesses such as HVAC, plumbing, roofing and equipment service shops (YC page); the company website in 2026 describes a physical AI lab building a robot Workcell
problem: Service shops lose work to missed calls, slow quotes and manual back office tasks. The earlier influencer marketing product targeted manual creator outreach.

founders.name: Robert Lukoszko
previous_startups: Fixkey.ai (acquired for six figures per the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page. A third party site names Alex Pokras as a co-founder, which no company source confirms.

technical_complexity.rationale: AI agents for outreach and operations are standard LLM engineering, while the later robot Workcell would add hardware difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Influencer outreach agents were easy to copy, and the company later changed direction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Stormy.

market_need_then: The launch posts framed influencer marketing as running on spreadsheets and manual DMs, and the product won Product Hunt Product of the Day on 2025-08-18.

identity.visual_style: Blog and content marketing heavy site

branding.brand_signature: Product Hunt Product of the Day, 2025-08-18
branding.community_and_virality: Reached number one on Product Hunt on 2025-08-18 with 643 upvotes per a Product Hunt tracker, and was covered by a Japanese outlet.

brand_strength.rationale: A Product Hunt win and press coverage show launch attention, but the product direction has changed since.

pivots.why: A founder interview says low level engineering for each advance did not scale for a small team. The date is not stated.

pivots.from: Influencer marketing agent and service business back office AI
pivots.to: Physical AI lab with a robot Workcell
pivots.why: Not stated. Inferred from the company website in November 2026, which describes only the lab and robot.

outcome_analysis: Stormy changed direction at least twice. It began with desktop agents, moved to an influencer marketing agent that won Product Hunt in August 2025, and the YC page describes service business AI while the 2026 website describes a physical AI lab. Funding reports conflict and no outcome is public.
notes: Funding conflicts: a search result titled stormy raises 1 7m is on the company's own blog (the page returned 404 when fetched, so only the title and URL were seen), CB Insights lists $1.6M on 2025-09-12 and $2.1M total, PitchBook lists $1.7M dated 2026-04 and $2.2M total, and a $500K 2024-09 seed is listed by aggregators. The round is recorded with a null date and stage seed as labeled by the headline, other figures unverified. Competitor pages (Avoca, ServiceTitan, Jobber) are dated 2026 and not near the batch, so competitors are left empty. Outcome search found no acquisition or shutdown. The YC launch post and the YC description do not match, and the website now differs again.
